findings: Both full guides document the same NPCI real-time transfer and India/INR customer context. The customer authenticates and approves via UPI app using desktop QR/mobile redirect; recurring AutoPay requires separate mandate approval before future automatic charges within mandate terms. Enable UPI through Dashboard for relevant methods on Stripe front ends, or use the separate manual integration route. Keep method selection and actual account eligibility separate.

Both guides list 35 identical business account countries, Connect, standard payout timing, full/partial refunds, no manual capture and 1–100,000 INR with a recurring cap of 15,000 INR. The source incorrectly counts 36. Both guides name Invoicing, Payment Links and Subscriptions as Dashboard paths without specifying collection methods.

Both guides retain the 60-day asynchronous refund window, up to seven business days and final `refund.updated`/`refund.failed` notifications. `succeeded` and `failed` are Refund states. Failure returns the amount to the merchant's Stripe balance and needs an alternative refund. The payer's bank/PSP decides on a dispute; acceptance makes it non-contestable and removes funds immediately.

reviewed_answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/upi, old raw lines 8-58 and new raw lines 9-59 preserve India customer location and INR presentment, UPI-app authentication and approval through desktop QR or mobile redirect, and separate recurring mandate authorization.
